prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthClientProvider._initialize() loads stored tokens from TokenStorage but never recomputes token_expiry_time from the token's expires_in, so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired stored token as valid. prs.title: fix(server): reject concurrent duplicate JSON-RPC request ids
prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same underlying bug: _handle_post_request keys _request_streams by str(request_id) with no uniqueness check, so a second concurrent request reusing the same JSON-RPC id silently overwrites the first request's routing slot, cross-wiring responses (one request receives the other's payload, the other hangs). #3063's own commit message references this as issue #3060. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same underlying bug: _handle_post_request keys _request_streams by str(request_id) with no uniqueness check, so a second concurrent request reusing the same JSON-RPC id silently overwrites the first request's routing slot, cross-wiring responses (one request receives the other's payload, the other hangs). #3063's own commit message references this as issue #3060. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3221 fixes a gap in #3063's own approach: #3063 keys on str(message.id), which collapses JSON-RPC int id 1 and string id "1" into the same key. #3221's diff explicitly calls this out ("Using str(id) collapses them so an in-flight numeric id falsely 409s a string id, or cross-wires responses") and introduces a type-preserving _request_stream_key() (i:/s: prefixes) instead. #3221 also closes an additional edge case #3063 doesn't handle: a string request id equal to the literal GET_STREAM_KEY ("_GET_stream") colliding with the standalone GET stream slot. Both add the same duplicate-id-rejection behavior, but #3221 is the more complete fix and should absorb #3063.

prs.title: fix(shared): make UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe
prs.author: ulofiai
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError subclasses (esp. UrlElicitationRequiredError) fail or lose data when pickled: the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is set by MCPError.__init__ to (code, message, data), which doesn't match subclass constructor signatures like UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None) — raising TypeError on unpickle (tracked as #2431). (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError subclasses (esp. UrlElicitationRequiredError) fail or lose data when pickled: the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is set by MCPError.__init__ to (code, message, data), which doesn't match subclass constructor signatures like UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None) — raising TypeError on unpickle (tracked as #2431). (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Fixes the bug generically on the MCPError base class: __reduce__ returns (_restore_mcp_error, (type(self), self.args), self.__dict__), reconstructing via MCPError.__new__ + Exception.__init__ + __dict__ restore rather than calling any subclass constructor. This covers every current and future MCPError subclass uniformly, and its test diff adds coverage for NoBackChannelError in addition to UrlElicitationRequiredError, showing the fix was verified across multiple subclasses. #2555 only adds a __reduce__ override on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so any other subclass with a constructor signature mismatch remains unfixed. #2478 instead adds a manual dispatch helper (_restore_mcp_error) that special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError vs. calls from_error_data for everything else — this requires updating the dispatch table for every future subclass with a custom constructor, and the posted diff never shows this helper actually wired into a __reduce__ method, so the fix appears incomplete as submitted.

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client ultimately fails (max attempts exhausted / underlying reconnection error), the pending tool call never receives a response and the transport gives no clear signal to the caller. #2395 patches the `if attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS` branch in `_handle_reconnection` to send a JSONRPCError (code INTERNAL_ERROR) on `ctx.read_stream_writer` so the specific pending request resolves instead of hanging. #3098 instead adds an `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull a `StreamableHTTPError` out of an anyio ExceptionGroup so that reconnection failure is raised as a clean exception rather than an opaque group — a different propagation mechanism (raised exception vs. in-band JSON-RPC error) for the same failure event. clusters.pick_reason: Fixes the bug generically on the MCPError base class: __reduce__ returns (_restore_mcp_error, (type(self), self.args), self.__dict__), reconstructing via MCPError.__new__ + Exception.__init__ + __dict__ restore rather than calling any subclass constructor. This covers every current and future MCPError subclass uniformly, and its test diff adds coverage for NoBackChannelError in addition to UrlElicitationRequiredError, showing the fix was verified across multiple subclasses. #2555 only adds a __reduce__ override on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so any other subclass with a constructor signature mismatch remains unfixed. #2478 instead adds a manual dispatch helper (_restore_mcp_error) that special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError vs. calls from_error_data for everything else — this requires updating the dispatch table for every future subclass with a custom constructor, and the posted diff never shows this helper actually wired into a __reduce__ method, so the fix appears incomplete as submitted.

clusters.pick_reason: #3221 fixes a gap in #3063's own approach: #3063 keys on str(message.id), which collapses JSON-RPC int id 1 and string id "1" into the same key. #3221's diff explicitly calls this out ("Using str(id) collapses them so an in-flight numeric id falsely 409s a string id, or cross-wires responses") and introduces a type-preserving _request_stream_key() (i:/s: prefixes) instead. #3221 also closes an additional edge case #3063 doesn't handle: a string request id equal to the literal GET_STREAM_KEY ("_GET_stream") colliding with the standalone GET stream slot. Both add the same duplicate-id-rejection behavior, but #3221 is the more complete fix and should absorb #3063.

members.title: fix(streamable-http): reject duplicate in-flight request ids
members.author: Sammy-Dabbas
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Both fix the same underlying bug: _handle_post_request keys _request_streams by str(request_id) with no uniqueness check, so a second concurrent request reusing the same JSON-RPC id silently overwrites the first request's routing slot, cross-wiring responses (one request receives the other's payload, the other hangs). #3063's own commit message references this as issue #3060.
